title: Starbucks wants to use AI to show you a ‘personalized digital menu’ at the drive-thru
slides: Starbucks bets your drive-thru order is about to get stranger
It's building AI menus that change per customer
The system decides what you see before you speak
Your usual order may quietly disappear from view
Ask yourself: who controls what you're shown next time?
thread_text:
1. The Menu Knows You

Starbucks is testing AI drive-thru menus that personalize what you see before you say a word.

2. Order Without Speaking

The system predicts your choice and displays it first — turning the menu into a suggestion engine.

3. Your Usual Vanishes

If the AI thinks something else fits better, your go-to drink may quietly disappear from the screen.

4. Who Sets the Menu?

The algorithm decides what's visible, which means it also decides what you're unlikely to consider.

5. Check Your Next Menu

Next time you order, ask: did I pick that, or did the screen pick for me? Try noticing the difference.

instagram.caption:
Your usual order might not be on the screen next time you pull up to the drive-thru.

Starbucks is building AI menus that change for each customer at the drive-thru. The system predicts your choice and shows it first, before you say a word. If the algorithm thinks something else fits better, your go-to drink can quietly disappear from view. ☕

For anyone who publishes or sells online, the lesson is bigger than coffee: whoever controls the display controls the choice. What you create matters less if an algorithm decides who sees it. 👀

Next time you order, ask yourself: did I pick that, or did the screen pick for me? 🤔
